title: A fresh start: what your shahada means
hook: You just made the biggest decision of your life. Let's make sense of it.

screens.text: **Welcome, {{convert.first_name}}.** You just made the biggest decision of your life, and {{masjid.name}} is glad you're here. Today: what you actually said, and what it means for you.
When you became Muslim, you said the **shahada**: the testimony of faith. **Allah** is simply Arabic for God. Arabic-speaking Christians and Jews call God "Allah" too [Field Guide ch. 4].

screens.arabic: أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱللَّٰهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ ٱللَّٰهِ
screens.translit: Ash-hadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan rasul Allah
screens.meaning: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah
screens.when: The words that made you Muslim. You'll also say part of them in every prayer.

screens.prompt: What does *la ilaha illa Allah* mean?
screens.answer: There is no god but Allah
screens.feedback: It's the heart of Islam: only Allah deserves worship.

screens.text: Those two sentences carry **three big beliefs**.
bubbles: **Guidance.** Allah sent messengers to show people how to live. **Muhammad ﷺ** was the last, and the Qur'an came through him.
**A next life.** Everyone will meet Allah and see what they did. *(ﷺ means "peace and blessings be upon him." Muslims say it after his name.)*

options.feedback: Yes. He was the final messenger, and the Qur'an came through him.
Not quite. Many messengers came before him. He was the last.
Not quite. Allah sent many messengers. Muhammad ﷺ was the last.

screens.text: **Your slate is clean.** The Prophet ﷺ told a man who was afraid of his past that Islam wipes out everything before it [Muslim 121]. The Qur'an says the same [Q 8:38].
bubbles: It even promises that Allah can turn past wrongs into good for those who believe and do good [Q 25:70].
Whatever you carried in, you don't carry it anymore.

screens.prompt: True, or a myth new Muslims often worry about?

items.text: Saying the shahada sincerely is what makes me Muslim
items.why: No witnesses needed. A masjid certificate only helps with paperwork later, like marriage or Hajj.

items.text: I have to change my name
items.why: Only if its meaning goes against Islam. Most names are fine, and you keep your family name.

items.text: I have to know everything right away
items.why: Even the Prophet ﷺ had people taught one step at a time. That's how this program works.

items.text: I have to drop my family and my old life
items.why: Islam asks you to be good to your parents, even if they disagree. Day 4 shows how.

items.text: I have to become Arab, or Pakistani, or someone else
items.why: Islam isn't an ethnicity. You keep your culture, food and style, minus anything Islam forbids.

items.text: The wrongs I did before Islam are wiped out
items.why: Islam wipes out what came before it [Muslim 121].

screens.text: **One thing before your first prayer: ghusl**, a full shower done as worship. You take it **once now**, as a new Muslim. It isn't something you repeat before every prayer: that's the short wash, wudu (Day 2).

screens.title: How to take your ghusl
screens.intro: {women}On your period? Take it once your period ends.{/women}

steps.text: Take off nail polish or anything waterproof on your skin
Intend it in your heart: this shower is for Allah
Wash your hands and private parts
Rinse your mouth and your nose
Wash your whole body, making sure water reaches the roots of your hair

screens.done_text: That's ghusl. It also counts as your wudu until something breaks it.

chips: What if I didn't say the shahada perfectly?
Do I have to tell anyone I'm Muslim?
Are my past sins really gone?

screens.prompt: What made you say yes to Islam? Write a sentence or two. This stays private. You'll come back to it on Day 23.

screens.text: Take your ghusl, and start your prayers.
steps: Take your ghusl, following the steps you just saw
In a quiet moment, say the shahada once more, just to yourself
Prayer starts today. If a prayer time comes before tomorrow, do Days 2 and 3 now: they're open, about seven minutes each
screens.optional_extra: If you'd like someone to show you wudu and prayer in person, {{mentor.name}} can.

screens.text: You testified that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad ﷺ is His Messenger. Your past is wiped clean, and you're still you.
That's Day 1. Next: getting ready to pray, then your first prayer. One step at a time.

check.prompt: What happens to the wrongs you did before Islam?

options.feedback: Right. Islam wipes out what came before [Muslim 121].

options.text: You have to make up for each one
options.feedback: Not quite. Islam wipes out what came before it [Muslim 121].

check.prompt: Do you need witnesses for your shahada to count?

options.text: No, saying it sincerely is enough
options.feedback: Right. A certificate only helps with paperwork later.
Not quite. Sincerity is what counts; witnesses are for paperwork.

check.prompt: Do you have to change your name when you become Muslim?

options.text: Only if its meaning goes against Islam
options.feedback: Right. Most names are fine, and you keep your family name.

options.text: Yes, everyone takes an Arabic name
options.feedback: Not quite. A new name is only needed if the meaning goes against Islam.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- The shahada, said sincerely with understanding and acceptance, is what makes someone Muslim. No witnesses are needed for it to count; a certificate is helpful for marriage, Hajj and other paperwork [SeekersGuidance, shahada witnesses].
- Islam wipes out what came before [Muslim 121; Q 8:38]. Those who repent, believe and do good can have past wrongs replaced with good [Q 25:70].
- Belief is learned in stages: the shahada first, then prayer, then the rest [Bukhari 1395; IslamQA 109201].
- A name change is required only if the name's meaning conflicts with Islam; family names are kept [IslamOnline (Siddiqi); IslamWeb 393040].
- A woman who converts during her period takes her ghusl when the period ends, and doesn't pray until then [Research Notes - Core Essentials §3 (AMJA/Zarabozo)].
- Before ghusl, anything waterproof on the skin or nails (nail polish) must come off, or the ghusl isn't complete [First Instructions on Worship, Part I].
- Ghusl: the Prophet ﷺ told Qays ibn 'Asim to bathe when he accepted Islam [Abu Dawud 355]. Scholars differ on whether it's required for every convert or only for those with prior major impurity, which covers almost every adult. All agree it isn't a condition for the shahada to count [IslamWeb 11140; Darul Ifta Birmingham 19848].

**Likely questions**
- *"What if I said it wrong or mispronounced it?"* Sincerity and meaning are what matter. If they want peace of mind, they can say it again any time; there's no harm.
- *"Do I have to tell people?"* No one is owed an announcement. Day 4 covers telling family safely. Their privacy is theirs.
- *"Are my past sins really gone?"* Yes [Muslim 121; Q 8:38]. Reassure warmly. Don't list categories of sin.
- *"When do I start praying?"* Prayer is due from now on. Days 2 and 3 are unlocked now and teach it; if a prayer is coming up, send them to Day 3. A ghusl also counts as wudu, so after it they can pray straight away unless something breaks their wudu; they'll still want Day 2's wudu steps for the next prayer. Offer to walk them through it. Never tell them prayer can wait.
- *"Do I need to be circumcised?"* It isn't a condition of being Muslim. Don't go further: escalate to the imam privately.
- *"What do I need to believe about Jesus?"* Brief: Muslims love and honor Jesus as a great prophet. Day 27 covers it.

**Escalate:** circumcision; a convert already married to a non-Muslim spouse (Q21); anyone asking about past marriages, inheritance or debts from before Islam.

**Don't**
- Don't tell them to change their name, cut off anyone, or adopt a new culture.
- Don't present ghusl as a condition of their Islam.
- Don't overload: no long lists of rules on Day 1.
madhabNote: Rinsing the mouth and nose is a required part of ghusl in the Hanafi and Hanbali schools, and recommended in the Maliki and Shafi'i schools. Doing it covers every school.
